memory_ras.note: Standard DRAM refresh — no performance impact.

memory_ras.note: Standard unencrypted DRAM operation (maximum memory performance).

memory_ras.note: System Management Interrupt triggers on correctable ECC errors, logging telemetry to BMC SEL for predictive failure analysis.

memory_ras.label: Max Performance Memory Frequency
memory_ras.note: DRAM bus locked to maximum rated frequency for peak memory bandwidth.

memory_ras.label: ECC Optimizer
memory_ras.note: Standard ECC — no capacity or bandwidth overhead. Recommended for vSAN.

memory_ras.label: PPR on UCE Enabled
memory_ras.note: DDR5 hardware DRAM row remapping active on uncorrectable ECC errors at boot. Automatically remaps faulty DRAM rows, preventing spurious server outages.

cpu_power.label: C-States Enabled
cpu_power.note: CPU can enter deep idle states. Acceptable for most workloads but adds wake-up latency for bursty vSAN IO.

cpu_power.label: Power Determinism
cpu_power.note: CPUs dynamically balance performance within socket power envelope (default). Consider Performance Determinism for ultra-low latency vSAN.

cpu_power.label: NPS1 (1 NUMA Node / Socket)
cpu_power.note: Single NUMA domain per socket. Optimal for very wide VMs spanning full socket memory; consider NPS4 for latency-sensitive workloads.

cpu_power.label: Custom Profile
cpu_power.note: Individual BIOS settings override profile defaults — verify C-States, Turbo, and SpeedStep manually.

cpu_power.label: CCX as NUMA Domain Disabled
cpu_power.note: NUMA domains mapped per socket or per die (NPS1). Recommended standard for general vSphere VM placement.

cpu_power.label: PCIe ASPM Disabled
cpu_power.note: PCIe link power savings disabled — keeps high-speed NVMe and 100GbE links at full readiness with zero wake latency. Recommended for vSAN ESA.

cpu_power.label: x2APIC Mode Enabled
cpu_power.note: Extended interrupt controller active. Required for systems with >255 logical processors.

side_channel.note: BIOS locks security configuration at POST to prevent runtime malware modification.

rules.rationale: System Profile is set to Custom (Custom). Allows OS-controlled power management (OS DBPM) as recommended by VMware Best Practices so ESXi Host Power Management can govern CPU frequencies and C-states.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: AMD NUMA Nodes Per Socket is set to NPS-1 (1). VMware vSphere 7.0 U2+ and vSphere 8/9 recommend NPS-1 (with CCX-as-NUMA deactivated) as the default setting for optimal performance across general-purpose virtualized workloads.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, AMD EPYC Processor NUMA Settings (p. 28)

rules.rationale: Intel VMD is Disabled. NVMe SSDs operate in native PCIe pass-through mode for direct ESXi kernel and vSAN ESA attachment.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, NVMe Storage (p. 17)

rules.rationale: PCIe ASPM is Disabled. High-speed PCIe links operate at full performance without link sleep wake latency.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Network Hardware Considerations (p. 19)

rules.rationale: CPU hardware-assisted virtualization (VT-x / AMD-V) is Enabled. ESXi hypervisor can schedule 64-bit guest workloads.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Hardware-Assisted Virtualization (p. 12, 21)

rules.rationale: Logical Processor (Hyper-Threading / SMT) is Enabled. All hardware execution threads are available to ESXi schedulers.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, General BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: System Boot Mode is UEFI. Fully compliant with VCF 9.1, UEFI Secure Boot, TPM 2.0 attestation, and NVMe boot devices.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Validate Your Hardware (p. 11)

rules.rationale: Processor C-States are Enabled (Enabled). VMware recommends activating all C-states in BIOS to allow ESXi Host Power Management full flexibility and maximize Turbo Boost frequency headroom on active cores when idle cores enter deep sleep states.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21–22)

rules.rationale: CPU Turbo Mode is Enabled. Processors dynamically boost to maximum all-core and single-core frequencies under load.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, General BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: SR-IOV Global Enable is Enabled in BIOS. PCIe NICs support hardware-assisted Virtual Functions (VFs).
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Network Hardware Considerations (p. 19)

rules.rationale: CPU Power Management is set to OS DBPM (OsDbpm). Allows ESXi Host Power Management to govern CPU dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS), aligning with VMware general virtualization recommendations.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: Processor C1E attribute not exposed in BIOS telemetry.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21–22)

rules.citation: AMD EPYC Performance Tuning Guide for VMware vSphere, Fabric Frequency (APBDIS)

rules.rationale: AMD Data Fabric C-States attribute not exposed in BIOS telemetry.
rules.citation: Dell PowerEdge BIOS Performance and Workload Tuning Guide, AMD Infinity Fabric

rules.rationale: AMD Determinism Slider is set to Power Determinism (PowerDeterminism). Dynamically maximizes core clock speeds within the socket power envelope. Suitable for general virtualization; consider Performance Determinism for ultra-low latency.

rules.rationale: Single-socket AMD server platform (e.g. PowerEdge R7715). Multi-socket xGMI interconnect links are not physically present; all communication occurs across local on-die Data Fabric.
